facts.subject: language
facts.text: Louis Braille invented the Braille reading system when he was only 15 years old.

facts.subject: language
facts.text: A palindrome is a word or phrase that reads the same backwards and forwards, like 'level'.

facts.subject: language
facts.text: The word 'quarantine' comes from an Italian phrase meaning forty days.

facts.subject: language
facts.text: Mandarin Chinese has more native speakers than any other language.

source.title: Wikipedia: List of languages by number of native speakers

facts.subject: math
facts.text: About 1,400 years ago, the Indian mathematician Brahmagupta wrote down rules for doing sums with zero.

facts.subject: math
facts.text: In the Fibonacci sequence, each number is the sum of the two numbers before it: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 ...

facts.subject: math
facts.text: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.

facts.subject: math
facts.text: The digits 0 to 9 that we use today are called Hindu-Arabic numerals and were developed in India.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen, which is why its chemical formula is H2O.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach the Earth.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: Diamonds and pencil lead (graphite) are both made of the same element: carbon.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: Africa has 54 countries.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: Indonesia is made up of more than 17,000 islands.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: The Great Wall of China is more than 20,000 kilometres long when all its sections are counted.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: Your brain uses about 20 percent of the energy your body makes, even though it is a small part of your body.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: Red blood cells carry oxygen around your body.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: A vaccine teaches your immune system to recognise a germ before you meet it.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: Your body has three kinds of muscle: skeletal muscle that moves your bones, smooth muscle in places like your stomach, and heart muscle.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: Phishing is when someone sends a fake message to trick you into giving away a password or other private information.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: A longer password is usually harder to guess than a short one with tricky symbols.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: Wikipedia is written and edited by volunteers.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: The first cash machine (ATM) was put into use in 1967.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: Inflation means that prices rise over time, so the same money buys less.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: The Riksbank in Sweden, founded in 1668, is the oldest central bank still working.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: A budget is a plan for how you will spend and save your money.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: A Rubik's Cube can be twisted into more than 43 quintillion different positions.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: A Venn diagram uses overlapping circles to show what different groups have in common.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: Confirmation bias is when we pay more attention to facts that agree with what we already believe.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: The board game Go has been played for more than 2,500 years.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa and also drew designs for flying machines.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: The composer Ludwig van Beethoven kept writing music even after he went deaf.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: A haiku is a short Japanese poem. In English, haiku often have three lines.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: The Taj Mahal, in India, was built from white marble by order of the emperor Shah Jahan.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: The programming language Python is named after the comedy group Monty Python.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: Grace Hopper helped create the first compiler, a program that turns code into instructions a computer can run.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: A pixel is the smallest dot that makes up a picture on a screen.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: An algorithm is a set of steps for solving a problem.
